equation: SVP = 0.61078 * exp((17.27*T) / (T + 237.3)) kPa; AVP = SVP * RH/100; VPD = SVP - AVP

guards.why_clamp: The tick grid cannot land exactly on 100% RH, so saturated air computes a VPD of about -1.4e-5 kPa. Negative drying power is not a thing; it renders as a bar below the axis and reads as a sensor fault rather than as rain.
guards.why_band: The registry conversion spans -45..130 C and -6..119 %RH, which is the raw tick range and NOT the sensor's physical range. Full-scale ticks compute a VPD of -52 kPa. Out-of-band is a broken or condensing sensor; derive.py gates on it, this module only reports it.

note: Expected values computed from the equation above using stdlib math only, NOT by calling soundings_gateway.vpd — the same independence rule test_ds18b20.cpp states for its CRC literals. A vector generated by the code under test agrees with itself no matter how wrong both are.

vectors.name: tomato band, cool morning — the low edge of the band
saturated air — VPD floors at zero, never negative
freezing point — exp(0), so SVP is the bare coefficient
below freezing — the curve stays valid, the air just holds almost nothing
bone dry — AVP vanishes and VPD is the whole SVP

out_of_band.name: zero ticks — the raw floor, below anything the sensor can physically be
out_of_band.why: -45 C is below the SHT45's -40 C floor and -6 %RH does not exist. Ticks at zero is a sensor that answered with nothing, not a very cold dry day.

out_of_band.name: full-scale ticks — computes a physically impossible negative VPD
out_of_band.why: Unclamped this yields VPD = -52.39 kPa. It is the clearest demonstration that the registry's tick conversion spans more than the sensor's physical range.
